prompt: The adverse effect of sugar on health is well known to the public now. Some believe that the government should control the amount of sugar people consume. Others think that it is the responsibility of an individual to monitor their sugar intake. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
essay:
The harmful effects of excessive sugar consumption are now well documented. Some people believe that governments should control how much sugar the public consumes, for example by taxing high-sugar products, whereas others argue that adults should make their own decisions while understanding the consequences. In my view, both sides are partly right. Governments should discourage excessive sugar consumption through measures such as taxes, but adults should ultimately be free to make their own choices.

Many children consume high-sugar products every day, which can lead to diabetes or obesity in the long term. Diabetes can affect their life permanently, as they may need to check their blood sugar three or four times a day, and later in life some may even lose a foot. Obesity affects their daily life through low energy, difficulty getting out of bed, breathing problems, and being physically unable to do everyday tasks. One way to protect children's health is to tax high-sugar products aimed at children, so that parents are less likely to buy products that harm them.

However, some adults use high-sugar products to get the energy they need for intense weightlifting, and taxing these products would be unfair to them. Unlike children, adults are capable of weighing the risks and deciding what is right for their own bodies. If governments begin controlling what adults eat, it could lead to further restrictions on personal freedom.

In conclusion, governments should protect children from the harmful effects of sugar, for example through taxes on products aimed at them. Adults, however, should remain free to make their own choices, as they are able to understand the consequences.
